question.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field in Two Dimensions
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+x \\  & =\frac{1+{x}^{2}}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
